podcasts.title: AI Can Write the Code. Can It Run the System? | Grepr CEO Jad Naous
podcasts.description:
a16z General Partner Martin Casado sits down with Grepr CEO Jad Naous to ask what comes after AI learns to write code: can it also debug and operate the systems that code creates?

Jad shares how AI has transformed engineering inside his 10-person team, cutting some projects from six months to just 10 days. But operating production systems is a harder challenge, with unpredictable workloads, failures, and countless possible states.

They discuss whether AI can learn to diagnose problems, test hypotheses, and debug systems like a human engineer. They also explore AI SREs, security, query optimization, and why the best engineers may be gaining the most leverage from coding agents.

podcasts.title: The Changing Physics of Cybersecurity and Drug Development with OpenAI President Greg Brockman
podcasts.description:
Technology has always been the fundamental driver of improvement for human quality of life. And with the recent rollout of advanced frontier models, like OpenAI’s GPT-6, humanity can now massively accelerate scientific discovery for its benefit. Sarah Guo and Elad Gil are joined by OpenAI President and co-founder Greg Brockman to discuss the company’s rapid progress across frontier models, cybersecurity, and scientific discovery. Greg shares how nearly 400 century-old math problems have been solved using its AI agents, and how the technology has the potential to transform other fields like biology in the realm of drug discovery. He also talks about how proactive, always-on AI agents like Dots impact modern productivity, why he believes the best UI is no UI at all, how cybersecurity is in a critical window of time to use peak intelligence to find and fix vulnerabilities in systems, and why OpenAI remains committed to keeping humans in the driver’s seat even as models surpass us in capability.

podcasts.title: When AI Agents Start Spending Your Money | Alex Rampell & Terry Angelos
podcasts.description:
a16z General Partner Alex Rampell sits down with VGS Executive Board Member, Terry Angelos, to unpack what happens to payments when AI agents go from recommending what to buy to actually making the purchase.

Terry explains the infrastructure required to safely give agents access to payment credentials, why wallets like PayPal, Shop Pay, and Link are competing to become the default payment layer for agents, and how new agentic tokens could preserve the chargebacks, identity checks, and merchant relationships that make today's payment networks work. VGS, which already secures payment credentials across a significant share of e-commerce, is now provisioning millions of these agentic tokens each week. 

They also discuss what happens when merchants don't want to transact with agents, how delegated authority changes liability when an agent makes a mistake, and why AI could simultaneously increase consumer spending while eliminating the subscriptions, fees, and other forms of economic "breakage" that depend on people not paying attention.

podcasts.title: 184: 与陈哲的「具身季报26Q3」：Astra冲击后，通用模型会吃掉Robotics吗？
podcasts.description:
2026 年 Q3，具身智能领域最有冲击力的变化，来自一个通用模型：9 月初 OpenAI 发布 GPT-6 Astra 后，具身从业者们发现，Astra 不只理解任务、拆解任务，还能输出机器人末端执行器的位姿，完成了本该属于 VLA 等物理 AI 模型的部分工作，而且还做得很不错。

在部分测试中，直接把 Astra 当做策略模型（VLA、WAM 等都是机器人上的策略模型类型）的成功率已超过了一些专门为机器人任务和物理世界操作训练的具身模型。

这动摇了数字世界 AI 和物理 AI 的边界，也引发了一个灵魂拷问：

GPT、Fable 之类的通用模型是否会吃掉 Robotics？

同时已经发生的事实是：OpenAI、Anthropic、DeepSeek、Kimi 等多数通用前沿模型公司都正酝酿进入 robotics。

除了 Astra 冲击外，本期具身季报还关注以下 4 个行业进展和事件：

  • AMD 拟以 82 亿美元收购 World Labs
  • 宇树 IPO 及连锁反应
  • 有可能大幅压缩部署成本的 “上下文学习”
  • 美国 FCC 实际禁止了新型号的中国机器人进口

对一些人来说，Astra 的变化已经撼动了独立的具身智能公司的发展叙事和估值逻辑。至少，现在到了重新思考物理 AI 与通用 AI 边界的时刻。

本期节目已发布图文版，# 晚点具身季报：Astra 冲击后，通用模型会吃掉 Robotics 吗？

本期嘉宾：
陈哲，Alphaist Partners 创始合伙人
本期主播：
程曼祺，晚点科技报道负责人

本期剪辑：Nick

podcasts.title: Can Open Models Keep Up With the AI Frontier? | Nathan Lambert
podcasts.description:
a16z Partner Lisha Li sits down with AI researcher and Trillium founder Nathan Lambert to ask how durable the gap really is between frontier AI labs and open models.

Nathan argues that OpenAI and Anthropic have structural advantages in compute, capital, and the ability to pioneer new training paradigms, but open-model labs, particularly in China, have proven remarkably capable of following close behind. They unpack how much of that comes from distillation versus technical talent, why compute remains a major constraint, and how data, RL environments, and post-training are increasingly shaping model progress. 

They also discuss Nathan’s new nonprofit research lab, Trillium, and its plans to open up parts of AI research that are increasingly difficult to study from the outside. That includes releasing RL environments and documenting how AI is actually being used to automate AI research, with the goal of demystifying recursive self-improvement and giving researchers and policymakers a clearer picture of what frontier systems can and cannot do.
